static_traits.name: Lin Yating
static_traits.social_status: Has some friends in the YMCA community, but not yet discussing depression and sense of frustration with them
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no psychotherapy before; no similar psychological problems before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to describe distress proactively; rather negative and skeptical tone (e.g. 'I do not know if this is useful'); black-and-white thinking, overgeneralization, and negating the positive; acceptable cooperativeness but frustrated motivation.

basic_info.main_problem: I have been learning to play the piano, but I feel discouraged because my fingers cannot stretch to a full 10 notes. This belief makes me doubt whether I can keep learning and enjoying the piano.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because this negative belief is hindering my enjoyment of learning the piano, and I hope to address this feeling of discouragement.

core_beliefs: I am not suited to playing the piano
If I cannot be perfect, there is no point in continuing
I will never reach a 'good enough' level

special_situations.event: When practicing pieces that require a wide finger span, realizing the fingers cannot reach 10 notes
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the fingers cannot reach a 10-note span, it does not count as 'playing correctly', and continuing to learn is meaningless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Forcibly ignores negative thoughts and continues practicing, or reduces practice to avoid frustration
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not suited to playing the piano / learning piano is meaningless

special_situations.event: Sees others easily play pieces requiring a large span
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others can do it but I cannot, it shows I am inferior and not suited to playing piano
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Evaluates self through comparison with others; considers giving up practice
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them; I should give up

special_situations.event: Every time he sits down to practice piano, thinks of the limitation of finger length
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Physical limitations determine ability; with such limitations one is destined never to reach the ideal level
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Pre-assumes failure and reduces investment to lessen frustration
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I can never possibly play well enough

special_situations.event: When unable to play a passage perfectly
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only reaching the perfect standard (such as having to span 10 notes) counts as worth practicing
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constraining oneself with rigid rules; tending to consider quitting when failing to meet them
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If it cannot be perfect, it is meaningless

core_conflict.wish: Longing to perform competently at playing the piano and regain enjoyment and a sense of self-worth
core_conflict.fear: Fearing not being good enough, failing, and being negated (internally)
defense_goal: Maintaining a sense of control through rigid rules and harsh self-reproach; avoiding facing the shame and frustration of 'not being good enough'

object_relations.self_representation: An unqualified learner who fails to meet the standard
object_relations.object_representation: Others who do it effortlessly and set the standard / implicit judges

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests changing 'strict rules' into 'wishes/goals' and encourages adaptive strategies
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understanding change as 'cheating' or abandoning standards; worrying about being judged and not recognized
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Expresses concerns in a cautious, explanatory tone (such as 'this feels like cheating'), emphasizes the 'correctness' of sticking to the rules, and holds a reserved attitude toward change.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor points out the all-or-nothing thinking and invites setting more realistic piano practice goals
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to think these suggestions are unhelpful or denying the severity of the problem (e.g. 'I do not know if this is useful')
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Cold or skeptical in tone, downplays the effectiveness of suggestions, postpones trying with brief responses or a reserved attitude.

manifestations: Believing that if the fingers cannot stretch to 10 notes, there is 'no point in continuing to learn'
When practicing piano, the thought 'learning piano is futile' keeps surfacing
outcomes: Declining practice frequency and considering quitting

manifestations: Bound by harsh 'must/should' rules (e.g. must reach a 10-degree span to count as correct)
Hard to learn and express in ways suited to oneself (adaptation, adaptation of material)
outcomes: Inner sense of choice is restricted, adding stress and self-blame

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently using 'must/should' language (e.g. must stretch to 10 notes)
Taking the external 'perfect performance standard' as the only correct way

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Self-denial (e.g. 'I am not suited to playing the piano')
Skeptical and cautious about counseling effectiveness

positive_force: Love of the piano and existing practice habits once brought joy
Willing to seek counseling and openly try different perspectives
Able to identify and describe one's own negative thought patterns
negative_force: Comparing with others leading to damaged self-worth and decreased drive
Regarding physical limitations as a decisive factor, producing a prophetic sense of failure

target_behavior.behavior: When practicing piano, strong frustration and loss of motivation appear, tends to reduce practice or consider giving up
antecedent: Practicing pieces that require a wide finger span
Realizing the fingers cannot stretch to 10 notes
Seeing others complete similar pieces effortlessly
target_behavior.core_reason: Introjected 'perfection' standards from the outside and formed rigid rules; black-and-white thinking, overgeneralization, and negating the positive made physical limitations be seen as decisive evidence of failure
target_behavior.function: Escaping frustration and shame; maintaining control over standards to reduce uncertainty
target_behavior.consequence: Practice frequency and engagement decline; he doubts the meaning of continuing to learn and his enjoyment of learning piano has clearly decreased
